cleanIntro: The Coach Gun is a break-action side-by-side. It has no field strip in the semi-auto sense. It comes apart into barrels, forearm and stock/frame, and Stoeger publishes nothing past that. This book names itself as the Coach Gun single trigger extractor model. The work is the two bores, the breech faces, the top of the frame, and the pivot pins and frame walls the barrels bear on. The choke tubes get a tightness check every 50 shots and a clean every 100.

steps.title: Break the action and take both shells out by hand
steps.action: Rotate the top lock lever to the right and swing the barrels down. On the extractor model the shells are lifted out of the chambers, not thrown clear, so they stay in the gun until you pick them out. Close the gun with one still sitting there and it is loaded again. Take both out and look through both chambers before you go any further.
steps.caution: On the automatic-safety version, opening the gun moves the safety to "S" by itself. On a manual-safety gun, push it to "S" yourself.
steps.quote: TO UNLOAD — Rotate top lock lever to right and open action. Shells will be automatically extracted from gun and may be removed by hand, or ejected (if the case).
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO UNLOAD, p.8

steps.title: Know which book this is
steps.action: Stoeger's cover and the caption over its parts diagram both name this book as the single trigger side-by-side extractor model, and its parts list shows one trigger. Stoeger publishes a separate book for the Coach Gun Supreme. If your Coach Gun has two triggers, or throws its empties clear of the breech, this book does not describe your trigger or extractor. The take-down below is the forearm and the barrels only.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — Parts diagram caption, p.2
steps.warn: This book covers the single trigger extractor model.

steps.title: Load only the shell size marked on the barrel
steps.action: Read the gauge and chamber length stamped on the barrel and use nothing else. A smaller-gauge shell can slide down a bigger bore and lodge there, leaving room for a correct shell behind it. A break-action has no feed mechanism to stop a wrong shell for you. Stoeger states the rule plainly for this gun, along with its steel-shot limit.
steps.quote: Special care should be taken to insure that gun is not loaded with any size other than marked on gun barrel.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — p.10
steps.warn: DO NOT SHOOT STEEL SHOT THROUGH A FULL CHOKED BARREL

steps.title: Forearm off
steps.action: Press the forearm latch forward and push the front of the forearm down and away from the barrels. It comes off as one assembly, and once it is off the barrels can come off the frame. Take it fully off before you try to lift the barrels. With the forearm still latched, lifting the barrels levers the forearm iron against the front of the frame.
steps.quote: TO REMOVE FOREARM ASSEMBLY — Press forearm latch forward. Push front of forearm assembly downward.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REMOVE FOREARM ASSEMBLY, p.8

steps.title: Barrels off the pivot pins
steps.action: With the forearm off and the action open, move the barrels down slightly so the two circular cuts on their underside come off the frame's pivot pins. Then lift them up and away. It is a short, deliberate unhooking, not a slide. Hold their weight as they come free so the muzzles do not swing down onto the bench.
steps.quote: TO REMOVE BARREL ASSEMBLY — Remove forearm assembly. Open action. Move barrel assembly downward slightly to disengage from pivot pins. Lift upward and remove from frame.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REMOVE BARREL ASSEMBLY, p.8

steps.title: Both bores from the breech
steps.action: Run each bore from the breech with a cleaning rod and soft, lightly oiled cloths. If a bore is leaded or plastic-fouled, scrub it with nitro solvent. Then wipe it out and leave only a very light film of oil. Heavy oil left in a bore is exactly what Stoeger tells you to clear out before loading.
steps.caution: In freezing weather, remove excess oil. If it needs lubricant, use dry graphite or another lubricant that will not thicken in the cold.
steps.quote: CLEANING AND CARE — Open action. Clean barrel bores with cleaning rod and soft, lightly oiled cloths. If necessary, scrub bores with nitro solvent. Wipe clean and re-oil very lightly.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — CLEANING AND CARE, p.8

steps.title: Top of the frame, breech faces, pivot pins
steps.action: Clean the top surfaces of the frame carefully. Dirt or residue there can stop the action closing all the way, and a Coach Gun that does not close fully will not fire. Keep the polished breech faces clean with a light film of oil. Put gun grease, not oil, on the wear points: the frame's front radius where the forearm iron bears, the pivot pins, and the inside frame walls the barrels touch.
steps.quote: Clean top surfaces of frame. Accumulation of dirt or residue in this area may restrict complete closing of action and prevent gun from firing.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — CLEANING AND CARE, p.9

steps.title: Oil-wipe the steel every time you handle it
steps.action: After handling the gun, wipe every steel part with an oily cloth. The moisture your fingers leave behind is invisible and is enough to start rust. After wet weather, dry the steel first and then oil-wipe it. A sudden temperature change, like bringing the gun in from the cold, can leave condensation on the steel too.
steps.quote: After handling gun, oil wipe all steel parts. Invisible “prints” of moisture can cause rust unless removed.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — CLEANING AND CARE, p.8

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrels, forearm and stock/frame are the three pieces the Coach Gun comes apart into. Stoeger stops there on purpose: it does not recommend going further unless a part needs repair or replacement. Everything that fouls in normal shooting can be reached now. Deep Clean covers the forearm iron, which does come out for cleaning, the choke tube schedule and the stock bolt.
steps.prose: Past that point, this gun goes to a gunsmith or back to the store, by the manual's own words.
steps.quote: Any disassembly of the side by side shotgun described in the Gun Owner’s Manual in not recommended unless necessary for repair or replacement of worn or damaged parts. Select a qualified gunsmith or return gun to store.
steps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — p.9

deepSteps.title: Forearm iron out of the wood
deepSteps.action: With the forearm off the gun, unscrew the front forearm screw and the rear forearm screw. Then pull the iron out of the wood and slide the forearm iron assembly clear. Keep the two screws apart, because the parts list shows a long screw and a short one. This is the one sub-assembly the Coach Gun's book opens, and only when the iron itself needs cleaning.
deepSteps.quote: TO REMOVE FOREARM IRON ASSEMBLY — Remove forearm assembly. Unscrew front forearm screw and rear forearm screw. Pull iron from forearm. Slide forearm iron assembly from forearm. Assemble in reverse.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REMOVE FOREARM IRON ASSEMBLY, p.8

deepSteps.title: Wash the iron in solvent, dry it, oil it sparingly
deepSteps.action: Wash the forearm iron assembly in solvent, dry it thoroughly, and re-oil it sparingly before it goes back into the wood. Keep it to a light film. Extra oil soaks into the forearm wood around the iron, and the extractor parts on the iron only need a film, not a coat. Put it back together in the reverse order you took it apart.
deepSteps.prose: While the halves are apart, grease the matching radius on the front of the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Should cleaning of parts of forearm iron assembly be required, remove assembly from forearm. Wash assembly in solvent, dry and re-oil sparingly.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — CLEANING AND CARE, p.8

deepSteps.title: Choke tubes: check at 50 shots, clean at 100
deepSteps.action: Every 100 shots, take the screw-in chokes out with the choke tube wrench. Clean each one inside and out with lubricating oil and a piece of flannel. Press each one firmly to the end of its seat as it goes back in. Between cleanings, check every 50 shots that the tubes are still tight, because a tube that backs out under recoil can damage itself and the barrel threads.
deepSteps.prose: Never change a choke tube on a loaded gun.
deepSteps.caution: Each time after 50 shots, verify if the SCREW-IN CHOKE is tightly set.
deepSteps.quote: Periodically (each time after 100 shots) remove the SCREW-IN CHOKE and clean internally a and externally using lubricant oil and a piece of flannel cloth.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — SHOTGUNS - screw-in choke instructions, p.17

deepSteps.title: If the stock has been off, the stock bolt has a limit
deepSteps.action: If the stock has ever been removed, take special care putting it back. Tighten the stock bolt to no more than 5 ft-lbs. Stoeger warns that overtightening the stock bolt can stop the gun working properly. A number that low is hard to judge by hand, so use a torque wrench.
deepSteps.prose: The book gives no stock removal procedure; this is only the limit for putting it back.
deepSteps.quote: The stock bolt should be tightened, to torque not exceeding 5 ft. lbs. Overtightening of stock bolt may adversely affect proper functioning of gun.
deepSteps.cite: OWNER'S MANUAL / COACH GUN SIDE BY SIDE SHOTGUN / SINGLE TRIGGER EXTRACTOR MODEL — UNKNOWN — no edition, revision code or part number is printed anywhere in the document — TO REASSEMBLE STOCK, p.8

cleaning.name: BORES & CHOKES
tasks: Clean both bores from the breech with a rod and soft, lightly oiled cloths; nitro solvent if fouled
Wipe clean and re-oil very lightly
Check choke tightness every 50 shots; remove and clean the tubes every 100
Never change a choke on a loaded gun
Do not shoot steel shot through a full choked barrel

cleaning.name: FRAME & LOCKUP
tasks: Clean the top surfaces of the frame; residue there can stop the action closing fully
Keep the polished breech faces clean and lightly oiled
Grease the frame's front radius where the forearm iron bears
Grease the pivot pins and the inside frame walls that touch the barrels

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Oil-wipe every steel part after handling; invisible moisture prints cause rust
After wet weather, dry the steel and oil-wipe it; watch for condensation after a sudden temperature change
In freezing weather, remove excess oil and use dry graphite or a lubricant that will not thicken

reassembly: Rotate the top lock lever to the right to hold the top lock open, then fit the two small circular cuts on the underside of the barrels onto the frame's pivot pins.
Hold that engagement and rotate the barrels upward until the action closes and the top lock latches.
Offer the forearm to the bottom of the barrels at a slight angle, match the radius on the forearm iron to the radius on the front of the frame, and press it upward until it latches.
Close the gun by holding the forearm in one hand and raising the stock with the other until it locks. Never force the barrels open or shut.
On a new gun the top lever may not return to dead centre after closing. Stoeger says that is deliberate room for the locking surfaces to wear in, not a fault.
fncheck: With no ammunition anywhere near the bench, look through both bores and confirm they are clear and no patch is left in either chamber. Open and close the action a few times: the barrels and forearm should stay together, the action should close fully without grit or force, and the top lever should latch every time. On the automatic-safety version, confirm the safety moves to "S" each time the action opens. If something does not work after a thorough clean, the gun goes to a qualified gunsmith or to Stoeger's service center, not further apart on the bench.
